bihar_raw_news.title: Jan Suraaj announces candidates for 5 Bihar Legislative Council seats
bihar_raw_news.content: Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor Prashant Kishor-led Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) on Sunday announced candidates for five Bihar Legislative Council constituencies, getting an early start on elections to eight graduates’ and teachers’ seats that are expected to be announced soon. The terms of members representing the eight constituencies — four graduates’ and four teachers’ seats — are due to expire in November. Jan Suraaj has already said it plans to contest all eight seats as part of its organisational expansion in Bihar. Announcing the candidates at a press conference, Kishor said Afaq Ahmed would seek re-election from the Saran teachers’ constituency. Ahmed had won the seat six years ago with Kishor’s support, before the former poll strategist launched Jan Suraaj as a political party. Divya Jyoti, a lawyer and academician-turned-politician who joined Jan Suraaj last week, will contest from the Patna teachers’ constituency. The seat is currently held by JD(U) chief spokesperson Neeraj Kumar. The party has named S P Rai as its candidate from the Darbhanga teachers’ constituency, while Ravindra Yadav will contest the Darbhanga graduates’ seat. Rajnish Ranjan has been fielded from the Kosi graduates’ constituency. Live Events The Legislative Council election is separate from the Bihar Assembly polls and will cover graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies spread across around 30 districts of the state. Unlike Assembly elections, the contests are decided by specialised electorates comprising eligible graduates and teachers. Candidates’ local influence, their standing among these voters and the organisational strength of their parties are expected to play an important role in the eight contests. With five candidates now declared, Jan Suraaj has three more nominees to announce if it goes ahead with its plan to contest all eight seats. Add as a Reliable and Trusted News Source Add Now! bihar_raw_news.title: Lost in Amritsar, found in Bihar : Stranger uses ChatGPT to reunite elderly Punjab man with family
bihar_raw_news.content: Pic courtesy: SNS Subscribe to Notifications An elderly Punjab man who went missing during a government-sponsored pilgrimage to Amritsar was reunited with his family after travelling by train to Bihar, where a stranger sheltered him for four days and used internet searches to trace his village, his family said. Chaman Lal, a resident of Fatehgarh Gujran village in Ludhiana district, had travelled to Amritsar on Sept. 11 under the Punjab government’s Mukh Mantri Tirath Yatra scheme to visit the Golden Temple. Lal, who has memory problems, became separated from other members of the group and wandered towards Amritsar railway station, according to his family. He then boarded a train bound for Bihar and eventually reached Gaya, they said. His grandson, Sukhchain Singh, travelled to Amritsar after being informed that Lal was missing and lodged a complaint with police. Family members and villagers also circulated Lal’s photograph on social media as the search continued. In Gaya, a local resident identified as Neeraj said he noticed Lal wandering near the railway station and asking for food. “He could not tell me his address. He could only remember the name of his village, Fatehgarh Gujran,” Neeraj said. Neeraj said he took Lal home, gave him food and allowed him to stay with his family while he tried to establish where the village was located. Lal spoke Punjabi, which led Neeraj to focus his search on Punjab. He said he used ChatGPT and other internet searches over several days before identifying Fatehgarh Gujran as a village near Machhiwara Sahib in Ludhiana district. “I kept searching for about three days. Once I found that the village was near Machhiwara, I decided to take him back myself,” Neeraj said. Neeraj travelled with Lal from Gaya to Ludhiana and then to Machhiwara, where he showed the elderly man’s photograph to local residents on Saturday. A local resident, Master Krishan Lal, recognised Lal from a missing-person photograph that had been circulated on social media and contacted his grandson. Sukhchain Singh then reached Machhiwara and was reunited with his grandfather. “We searched for him in Amritsar but could not find him. I am extremely thankful to Neeraj for keeping my grandfather safe and bringing him back,” Singh said. Neeraj said he works in the construction sector in Gaya and has been helping people in distress since his school days. “When I saw him alone at the station, I felt I should help him,” he said. national_raw_news.title: Several Indian athletes begin medal hunt today at 20th Asian Games 2026 6 mins ago 5
national_raw_news.content: The 20th Asian Games 2026 will see several Indian athletes begin their medal hunt across multiple disciplines today. Indian shooters Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod will aim for podium finishes in the women’s 10m air rifle event. The trio will compete for both individual and team medals. The Indian women’s hockey team will also begin its campaign today, facing Uzbekistan in its opening group-stage match. The men’s hockey team will take on Indonesia in their first match of the tournament. In today’s cricket event, the Indian women’s team will face Bangladesh in the semifinal. The knockout match will start at 10:30 AM IST at the Aichi Prefectural Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin, Japan. The Indian teqball player Quimcy Dsouza missed out on a women’s singles bronze medal after suffering a 2-0 defeat to home favourite Yuina Sakamoto in a closely contested match. Sakomoto prevailed 12-11, 12-11 in a match that saw both games go down to the wire, leaving Dsouza to rue several missed opportunities. The Indian had chances to take control of the contest, holding set point in the opening game before Sakamoto fought back. Dsouza also established a lead in the second game and even saved a match point with a winning serve, but was unable to close out the contest as Sakamoto capitalised on crucial errors at the decisive moments. However, Dsouza will have another opportunity to claim a medal as she is set to compete in the mixed doubles bronze medal match alongside Mohamed Anas Beg.

national_raw_news.title: BJP Punjab’s ‘Nasha Mukt Punjab Yatras’ got remarkable response from people of state 30 mins ago 15
national_raw_news.content: Bharatiya Janata Party(BJP) Punjab’s “Nasha Mukt Punjab Yatras”, which the party’s National President, Nitin Nabin, launched from the border district of Pathankot on September 18th, is getting a remarkable response from the people of the state. Yesterday, Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, while launching the second out of four phases of the Yatras from Fatehgarh Sahib, termed it a movement of a new beginning in Punjab. She said ‘Nasha Mukt Punjab Yatra’ is not merely a political programme but a call for collective action to free Punjab from drugs, crime and fear. This 13-day long ‘Nasha Mukt Punjab Yatra ’, which has started with a tagline of – ‘Bhajpa Da Naara – Nasha Mukana Saara’ is focusing on three major challenges presently confronting Punjab. These are the growing drug menace, deteriorating law and order, and corruption at every level of governance. The Yatra will cover 4000 kilometres in the state to mobilise people from across all 117 Assembly constituencies to turn the fight against drugs into a mass public movement. The third yatra will be launched today by Union Minister of State for Law and Justice, Arjun Ram Meghwal, from Fazilka’s Sadiqi border, and tomorrow, the fourth phase will be flagged off by Union Agriculture Minister, Shivraj Singh Chouhan, and Haryana Chief Minister, Nayab Singh Saini, from Talwandi Sabo in Bathinda. The ‘Nasha Mukt Punjab Yatra’ will conclude on September 30th at Jalandhar, in which Union Home Minister Amit Shah is scheduled to participate.

national_raw_news.title: Three-Day IAF Air Show To Be Held In Varanasi In October, PM Modi Likely To Attend
national_raw_news.content: Varanasi Gears Up For Three-Day IAF Air Show Over Ganga, PM Modi Likely To Attend States Three-Day IAF Air Show To Be Held In Varanasi In October, PM Modi Likely To Attend Swarajya Staff Sep 20, 2026 | Updated 12:27 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Three IAF Rafales flying in formation. (Via PIB) Varanasi is set to witness its first-ever air show as the Indian Air Force (IAF) prepares to stage a spectacular three-day aerial display over the sacred Ganges. Scheduled for 22, 23 and 25 October, the event is expected to draw crowds of 20 lakh people to witness fighter jets and helicopters performing above the historic ghats stretching from Namo Ghat to Assi Ghat. The Indian Air Force plans to deploy more than three dozen aircraft for the show, including Rafale fighter jets, the renowned Suryakiran aerobatic team, Rudra helicopters, C-295 aircraft, Tejas fighters and Dakota aircraft. Performances will take place between noon and 2pm each day, with displays lasting approximately 90 minutes as three to five aircraft showcase aerial manoeuvres simultaneously over the river. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to attend as chief guest on the final day, with Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and senior military officials also likely to participate. Air Force authorities have coordinated extensively with Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport officials, with Suryakiran jets taking off from Varanasi Airport whilst other aircraft will fly from surrounding districts. District administration has begun preparations to manage the anticipated crowds, with special arrangements being made across 84 ghats along the riverfront. Namo Ghat, designated as the main control centre, will be handed over to Air Force control from 16 October, with public access restricted during the setup period. Officials have enlisted support from neighbouring Chandauli, Ghazipur and Jaunpur districts to handle crowd management and security. Rehearsals for the historic event will commence on 20 October and continue through 22 October. The Rajghat bridge and boat services on the Ganges will remain closed during performances for safety reasons. Local authorities are preparing for crowds comparable to the Dev Deepavali festival, with arrangements for approximately 5,000 VIP guests from across India and abroad.
